title: PTE Academic Listening — Practice Test 55
topic: Mixed academic topics (one per item, as in the real test)
instructions: Each item has its own recording. Audio plays automatically when you reach an item.

questions.audioScript: Microplastics are plastic particles smaller than five millimeters that have become widespread ocean pollutants. They originate from broken-down larger plastics, synthetic textiles, and industrial processes. Marine animals consume microplastics, mistaking them for food. These particles accumulate in fish tissues and bioaccumulate up the food chain. Research shows microplastics in human blood, suggesting dietary ingestion through seafood. Reducing plastic production and improving waste management are critical to controlling microplastic pollution.
questions.modelAnswer: Microplastics smaller than five millimeters have become widespread ocean pollutants from broken plastics and textiles. Marine animals consume them, confusing them with food. Microplastics bioaccumulate up the food chain and appear in human blood. Reducing plastic production and improving waste management are essential to controlling pollution.

questions.topic: The Printing Press and Information Revolution
questions.prompt: Item 2: The Printing Press and Information Revolution
questions.audioScript: Johannes Gutenberg's printing press, developed around 1440, revolutionized information distribution. Before printing, scribes laboriously copied texts by hand, making books expensive and rare. The press enabled mass production of identical copies, democratizing knowledge. Within fifty years, millions of books were printed across Europe. This accelerated the Renaissance and Protestant Reformation by spreading new ideas rapidly. The printing press fundamentally changed society by making information accessible to broader populations.
questions.modelAnswer: Gutenberg's printing press around 1440 revolutionized information distribution by enabling mass production. Before printing, scribes hand-copied texts, making books expensive and rare. The press democratized knowledge and spread new ideas quickly, accelerating the Renaissance and Protestant Reformation. This technology fundamentally changed society.

questions.audioScript: The Great Pyramids of Giza remain monumental achievements of ancient engineering. The Great Pyramid of Khufu required approximately 20 years to construct using 2.3 million stone blocks. Workers quarried limestone blocks weighing up to 2.5 tons. Construction methods likely involved ramps, levers, and organized labor systems. Precise geometric alignment demonstrates advanced mathematical knowledge. These structures served as monumental tombs housing pharaohs and treasures. Archaeological evidence suggests tens of thousands of workers participated in construction.
questions.question: According to the speaker, which TWO claims about the pyramids are supported?
options: Construction used only 100,000 stone blocks
The Great Pyramid required 20 years to build
Individual blocks weighed up to 2.5 tons
Construction methods were entirely mysterious
Precise alignment shows mathematical knowledge
correctAnswers: The Great Pyramid required 20 years to build
questions.explanation: The speaker explicitly states the 20-year construction period and describes precise geometric alignment demonstrating mathematical knowledge.
questions.prompt: Item 3: Ancient Egyptian Pyramids and Construction

questions.audioScript: Antibiotic resistance develops when bacteria survive antibiotic exposure through genetic mutations or acquired resistance genes. Overuse of antibiotics in medicine and agriculture accelerates resistance development. Some bacteria now resist multiple antibiotics simultaneously, becoming methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. Resistant bacteria can transfer genes horizontally to other bacterial species. Resistance mechanisms include enzyme inactivation of antibiotics and altered bacterial cell walls. Reducing unnecessary antibiotic use and developing new antibiotics are crucial strategies against resistance.
questions.question: According to the speaker, which TWO factors contribute to antibiotic resistance?
options: Antibiotic resistance cannot develop through mutations
Bacteria acquire resistance genes and mutations
Overuse of antibiotics accelerates resistance
Resistance genes transfer only vertically to offspring
No bacteria can resist multiple antibiotics
correctAnswers: Bacteria acquire resistance genes and mutations
questions.explanation: The speaker describes resistance developing through mutations and acquired genes, and explicitly states overuse accelerates this development.
questions.prompt: Item 4: Antibiotic Resistance and Bacterial Evolution
Item 5: Solar Energy and Photovoltaic Technology
questions.audioScript: Solar photovoltaic cells convert light energy directly into electricity through the photovoltaic effect. Silicon-based cells dominate commercial production due to abundance and established manufacturing processes. An individual cell produces a small voltage, so cells are connected in series to increase output power. Modern solar panels achieve approximately 15-20 percent efficiency in converting incident light to usable electricity, though laboratory prototypes demonstrate higher potential.
questions.transcript: Solar photovoltaic cells convert light energy directly into electricity through the __1__ effect. Silicon-based cells dominate commercial production due to abundance and established manufacturing processes. An individual cell produces a small voltage, so cells are connected in __2__ to increase output power. Modern solar panels achieve approximately 15-20 percent efficiency in converting incident light to usable electricity, though laboratory prototypes demonstrate __3__ potential.

questions.audioScript: Fossils are preserved remains or traces of ancient organisms providing evidence of evolutionary change. Body fossils preserve actual skeletal material, while trace fossils record organism activities like footprints and burrows. Radiometric dating methods measure the decay of radioactive isotopes to determine fossil age. Transitional fossils show intermediate stages between species, such as the famous Archaeopteryx with both reptilian and bird characteristics.
questions.transcript: Fossils are preserved remains or traces of ancient organisms providing evidence of __1__ change. Body fossils preserve actual skeletal material, while trace fossils record organism activities like footprints and burrows. Radiometric dating methods measure the decay of radioactive isotopes to determine fossil __2__. Transitional fossils show intermediate stages between species, such as the __3__ Archaeopteryx with both reptilian and bird characteristics.

questions.prompt: Item 7: Enzyme Catalysis and Metabolic Rates
questions.audioScript: Enzymes are biological catalysts accelerating metabolic reactions by lowering activation energy requirements. Each enzyme has an optimal pH and temperature at which maximum activity occurs. Substrate molecules bind to the enzyme's active site, forming a complex that undergoes chemical transformation. Enzyme inhibitors can reduce activity by blocking the active site or interfering with allosteric mechanisms essential for catalysis.
questions.transcript: Enzymes are biological catalysts accelerating metabolic reactions by lowering __1__ energy requirements. Each enzyme has an optimal pH and temperature at which maximum activity occurs. Substrate molecules bind to the enzyme's __2__ site, forming a complex that undergoes chemical transformation. Enzyme inhibitors can reduce activity by blocking the active site or interfering with __3__ mechanisms essential for catalysis.

questions.audioScript: Metamorphic rocks form when existing rocks undergo chemical and physical changes due to heat, pressure, or chemical alteration deep within Earth's crust. High pressure and temperature cause mineral rearrangement without melting the rock. Parent rocks include sedimentary and igneous types. Examples include marble from limestone and schist from shale. Metamorphic rocks contain distinctive mineral alignments reflecting directional pressure. These rocks mark ancient collision zones and deep crustal processes.
options: Metamorphic rocks form from existing rocks altered by heat and pressure deep in Earth, producing distinctive mineral alignments.
Metamorphic rocks form when sedimentary rocks melt completely into magma, then recrystallize near the surface.
All metamorphic rocks contain fossils unchanged from their parent rocks despite extreme geological conditions.
questions.correctAnswer: Metamorphic rocks form from existing rocks altered by heat and pressure deep in Earth, producing distinctive mineral alignments.
questions.explanation: The speaker explains metamorphic rocks result from heat and pressure altering parent rocks without melting, creating distinctive structures.

questions.prompt: Item 9: Ecosystem Succession and Climax Communities
questions.audioScript: Ecological succession describes predictable changes in community composition over time. Primary succession begins with bare rock where lichens colonize first, weathering rock into soil. Secondary succession follows disturbance in existing ecosystems, with pioneer species reestablishing quickly. As soil develops and shade increases, different species replace pioneers. Eventually, climax communities stabilize with mature species composition. Disturbances restart succession cycles, preventing permanent climax states in many ecosystems.
options: Ecological succession involves predictable species replacement from pioneer to climax communities, with early colonizers altering conditions enabling later species.
Ecological succession never occurs in nature; ecosystems remain unchanged for millions of years once established.
Climax communities develop rapidly after disturbances through simultaneous arrival of all mature species.
questions.correctAnswer: Ecological succession involves predictable species replacement from pioneer to climax communities, with early colonizers altering conditions enabling later species.
questions.explanation: The speaker describes succession as predictable community changes with pioneering species preparing conditions for later species.

questions.audioScript: Web accessibility ensures people with disabilities can use digital content effectively. WCAG guidelines establish standards for perceivable, operable, understandable, and robust web design. Alt text describes images for screen reader users unable to see visuals. Keyboard navigation allows interaction without a mouse. Color contrast requirements aid visually impaired users. Captions assist deaf and hard-of-hearing users. Accessible design benefits all users including those in noisy environments or using mobile devices.
questions.question: What is a key benefit of implementing web accessibility standards?
options: Accessibility decreases website functionality for majority users
Accessible design serves disabled users exclusively with no benefits for others
Accessibility standards improve usability for all users including those with temporary limitations
Web accessibility is too expensive to implement for any website
questions.correctAnswer: Accessibility standards improve usability for all users including those with temporary limitations
questions.explanation: The speaker notes that accessible design benefits disabled users and provides advantages for all users.

questions.audioScript: Digestion breaks food into absorbable molecules through mechanical and enzymatic processes. Saliva begins carbohydrate digestion with amylase. The stomach's pepsin breaks down proteins into polypeptides. Pancreatic enzymes in the small intestine complete carbohydrate, protein, and fat digestion. Bile salts emulsify fats enabling lipase digestion. The small intestine's absorptive epithelial cells move nutrients into the bloodstream. Intestinal motility called peristalsis propels food along the digestive tract.
questions.question: Where does most nutrient absorption occur in the digestive system?
options: In the stomach through absorption of partially digested food
In the small intestine through absorptive epithelial cells
In the mouth where saliva begins digestion
In the large intestine where water absorption occurs
questions.correctAnswer: In the small intestine through absorptive epithelial cells
questions.explanation: The speaker identifies the small intestine's epithelial cells as the primary site of nutrient absorption.
questions.prompt: Item 11: Enzymatic Digestion and Nutrient Absorption
Item 12: Healthy Aging and Preventive Medicine
questions.audioScript: Aging well requires maintaining physical activity, cognitive engagement, and strong social connections. Regular exercise preserves muscle, bone density, and cardiovascular health. Cognitive activities like learning new skills maintain mental acuity. Social interactions provide emotional support and cognitive stimulation. Preventive screenings catch diseases at early stages. Mediterranean diet patterns show protective effects against age-related disease. People prioritizing these factors experience improved healthspan, living longer in good …
options: health
wellbeing
vitality
function
questions.explanation: The speaker states these practices extend healthspan, living longer in good health.

questions.audioScript: Diverse teams bring varied perspectives improving problem-solving and innovation. Inclusion practices ensure all voices are heard in decision-making. Underrepresented groups face systemic barriers requiring intentional organizational efforts. Mentoring programs support career advancement for underrepresented professionals. Transparent hiring practices reduce unconscious bias. Companies with strong diversity and inclusion initiatives experience better financial performance and employee satisfaction.
options: performance
productivity
results
outcomes
questions.explanation: The speaker states diverse and inclusive companies experience better financial performance.

questions.audioScript: The internet revolutionized communication by connecting computers worldwide into a global network. Packet switching enables data to travel efficiently across multiple routes. Protocols standardize how devices exchange information reliably between distant locations.
questions.displayTranscript: The internet revolutionized communication by connecting computers worldwide into a local network. Packet switching enables data to travel slowly across multiple routes. Protocols standardize how devices exchange information poorly between nearby locations.
questions.explanation: The audio says global, efficiently, reliably and distant.

questions.audioScript: Enzymes accelerate chemical reactions by lowering activation energy requirements. Each enzyme has an optimal temperature and pH at which it works best. Extreme conditions can denature the protein and destroy its catalytic activity.
questions.displayTranscript: Enzymes accelerate chemical reactions by raising activation energy requirements. Each enzyme has an optimal temperature and pH at which it works worst. Extreme conditions can strengthen the protein and enhance its catalytic activity.
questions.explanation: The audio says lowering, best, denature and destroy.

questions.correctAnswer: Neural plasticity allows the brain to reorganize and form new connections throughout life.
